As the new school year begins, more Americans now support banning students from using phones entirely during class.

The new school year is underway, and support for banning iPhones in classrooms continues to grow.

Yes, it's still July, but summer break has somehow already come to an end. My kids head back to school today and tomorrow, marking the second summer in a row that the first day of school no longer falls in August.

Apple is welcoming the new school year with its annual "Back to School" promotion, offering eligible students and educators gift cards valued up to US$150 on select Mac and iPad purchases made before August 27. Consumers in certain states can also take advantage of limited-time sales tax holiday offers.

While back-to-school discounts are a pleasant surprise, phone use during class hours is increasingly unpopular.

Top Liked Comment by GreenPizza

I have not seen any data to support that allowing students to use phones reduces risk during school shootings. In reality, reducing classroom distractions is what truly lets us fulfil the purpose of going to school.

A new survey from the Pew Research Center found that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using phones during class. That's up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025. Just 18% now oppose a classroom ban.

Support for the stricter, all-day ban covering the entire school day is rising even faster. For the first time, more Americans support than oppose banning phones for the full school day.

The report also notes that younger adults remain less enthusiastic about both classroom and all-day bans, though support has risen across all age groups since 2024. You can read the full report here.

What do you think? Should schools limit iPhone use to class time only, implement an all-day ban, or leave the decision to students and parents? Let us know in the comments.
